title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take a rickshaw, bus or train, and give instructions politely or informally.
intro:
Getting around in Maharashtra means rickshaws (रिक्षा), crowded buses, Mumbai's local trains and a lot of asking the way. Directions are given with commands — सरळ जा 'go straight', डावीकडे वळा 'turn left' — so this unit teaches the **imperative** in its informal and polite forms.

You'll also learn the case endings for movement: **-ला** 'to', **-हून / -ऊन** 'from', **-पर्यंत** 'as far as', **-कडे** 'towards' and **-ने** 'by (bus, train)'.

grammar.title: Imperatives: जा, जा; ये, या
grammar.body:
**Informal (तू):** the bare stem: **कर** 'do', **थांब** 'wait', **बस** 'sit', **जा** 'go', **ये** 'come', **घे** 'take', **दे** 'give'.

**Polite (तुम्ही):** stem + **-आ**: **करा**, **थांबा**, **बसा**, **जा**, **या** (ये → या), **घ्या**, **द्या**. This is the standard form for strangers, elders, drivers, shopkeepers.

**Negative:** stem + ऊ + **नकोस** (informal) / **नका** (polite): जाऊ नकोस / जाऊ नका 'don't go'.

**'Let's':** stem + **ऊया** (or ऊ): चल, जाऊया 'come on, let's go'; बसूया 'let's sit'.

Soften with **ना** or **जरा** ('a bit'): जरा थांबा ना 'please wait a moment'.

examples.en: It's late, come on, let's go.

grammar.title: Movement: to, from, as far as, by
grammar.body:
Motion endings attach to the oblique form of the noun:

**-ला** 'to': मुंबईला जाणे 'to go to Mumbai', स्टेशनला 'to the station'
**-त / -मध्ये** 'into': दुकानात जा 'go into the shop'
**-कडे** 'towards; to (a person's place)': डॉक्टरकडे, मामाकडे
**-हून / -ऊन** 'from': पुण्याहून 'from Pune', घरून 'from home'
**-तून** 'out of, through': खिडकीतून 'through the window'
**-पर्यंत** 'as far as, until': स्टेशनपर्यंत
**-ने** 'by (means)': बसने 'by bus', ट्रेनने 'by train'; on foot = **चालत**

The postposition in 'from here / there' is fused: **इथून** 'from here', **तिथून** 'from there', **कुठून** 'from where'.

examples.en: Drop me as far as the station.
Let's go to uncle's place in the evening.

dialogue.title: Finding Shaniwar Wada
dialogue.setting: Jenny, a tourist in Pune, asks a passer-by the way to the historic Shaniwar Wada fort.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.en: Excuse me, where is Shaniwar Wada?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: Shaniwar Wada? It's quite close from here.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: At the second crossroads turn left.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.native: मग पाच मिनिटं चाला. उजवीकडे मोठा दरवाजा दिसेल.
lines.roman: mag pāts miniṭaṃ tsālā. udzvīkaḍe moṭhā darvādzā disel.
lines.en: Then walk five minutes. You'll see a big gate on the right.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.en: How long will it take on foot?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.en: Ten or fifteen minutes. Otherwise take a rickshaw.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.native: नाही, मी चालत जाते. खूप धन्यवाद!
lines.roman: nāhī, mī tsālat dzāte. khūp dhanyavād!
lines.en: No, I'll walk. Thanks a lot!

culture: To hail a rickshaw you don't say where you want to go and wait for a price — you ask **'…ला येणार का?'** ('will you come to …?'). Drivers may refuse short or out-of-the-way trips. In Mumbai, rickshaws run only in the suburbs; in the south of the city it's black-and-yellow taxis. Landmarks matter more than street names: people will direct you 'past the temple, near the medical shop'.
